- Confirmation that Redwood can commit to the SCCs in Appendix A as drafted (we redlined in the attached).

- Retention on termination: we proposed a 30-day secure deletion window; please confirm.

We appreciate a quick read and potential mark-ups from your legal ops so we can keep procurements on track.

Subject: Re: Initial DPA redlines + SCCs (Medix / Redwood)

Marissa / Karthik — I reviewed Medix's redlines + TIA. I attached a consolidated set of counter-redlines (Redwood_SCCs-approved-text.docx) with commentary. Summary of positions and suggested language: 

1) SCCs: We accept the standard module 2/3 text but propose an extra paragraph in the Annex on key-management assurance. Wording calls for HSM-backed KMS or equivalent controls for EU-hosted keys.

2) Roles and subprocessor notice: Accept Processor role. Counter-proposal: 15 business days notice for new subprocessors for EU-hosted data with a right for Medix to object within that window; if objected, we will provide a documented mitigation or offer an alternative hosting partition. (This shortens notice but adds mitigation.)

3) Retention / deletion on termination: We can commit to returning/deleting customer data within 30 days, with the caveat that immutable backups may be retained for an additional 90 days for recovery and compliance, but will be isolated and encrypted. We will add explicit language about forensic/legal holds overriding deletion.

4) Audit evidence: We can provide SOC2 Type II report and targeted KMS configuration summary under NDA — propose a bilateral NDA addendum and a secure evidence room (Drive link below).

5) TIA items: Most items are operational mitigations; we can accept the transfer addendum if Medix accepts the KMS/Audit trade-offs above.

Suggested immediate ask: quick alignment call with Medix legal and our security lead (Ben) early next week. If Ben confirms commercial terms are unchanged, we can ship a consolidated DPA with placeholders for the evidentiary artifacts.

Attachments: Redwood_SCCs-approved-text.docx
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2c-example-Redact

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Thanks, all. Medix legal has reviewed the counter-proposals. Quick summary:
- SCCs: agreeable to standard text plus a short KMS assurance annex; Medix requests specific phrasing to avoid "equivalent" being too subjective.
- Subprocessor notice: Medix prefers 30 calendar days but can accept 15 business days only if Redwood commits to a documented mitigation and a named escalation contact.
- Deletion: Medix asked that the backup carve-out be limited to 60 days rather than 90; they want assurance that encrypted backups cannot be used for new processing.

We are open to a quick call to finalize language. Can Ben's engineer join Tue 19 May 9 AM PT? We'll aim to resolve the last open items and get a final DPA signed next week.

Regards,
Sarah Lin
Head of Privacy Operations
Medix Solutions

- Replaces "equivalent" with a short list of acceptable KMS controls (HSM or cloud KMS with customer key isolation),
- Sets subprocessor notice to 15 business days with an express escalation path and named contact (Ben),
- Adjusts backup retention carve-out to 60 days and adds an explicit prohibition on using backups for active processing.

If Medix agrees to that wording on the call we can finalize and push the DPA + SCC appendix into DocuSign for signature the same day. Appreciate the quick turnaround on your side.

Best,
Marissa
